newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Spectre of liquidation stalks Fokker - minister.
newsitem.headline: Spectre of liquidation stalks Fokker - minister.

text.p: Bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker faces liquidation next year unless a saviour unexpectedly emerges to keep the company alive, Minister of Economic Affairs Hans Wijers told reporters on Thursday.
"If no serious candidate comes forward then liquidation becomes inevitable at a certain moment," he said.

Wijers was speaking after news that Short Brothers of Belfast was no longer willing to supply wings to Fokker and that the Dutch company's court-appointed administrators had broken off exclusive takeover talks with Samsung Aerospace.
Wijers told a news conference that he continued to hold out hope that a saviour may yet emerge, but added that the prospect of a rescue deal for Fokker was becoming increasingly remote.
"You must never rule out the possibility of other candidates emerging...But I must say the chances have become much smaller as a result of the events of the last few weeks," he said.
Fokker would continue work on a handful of outstanding orders until May 1997, but a fire-sale of its assets would be inevitable if a rescue deal had not been completed by then.
"Then the administrators will try to sell the assets of the company in a manner which best serves the interests of the creditors," he said.

Asked if any companies other than Samsung had expressed an interest in acquiring Fokker, Wijers gestured in front of himself and said: "I'll have a look at the table, since you ask, but I still don't see anything."
